title: A bill to require the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study on disparities associated with race and ethnicity with respect to certain benefits administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This bill requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a study to assess whether there are disparities associated with race and ethnicity with respect to (1) compensation benefits administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), (2) disability ratings determined by the VA, and (3) the rejection of fully developed claims for VA benefits. The GAO must also develop recommendations to facilitate better data collection on such disparities associated with race and ethnicity.

Within one year, the GAO must brief Congress on the initial results of the study. The GAO must also submit a final report on the study following the briefing.

summary.headline: Requires the GAO to study whether race and ethnicity create unequal outcomes in certain VA benefits and claims.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Government Accountability Office, a federal watchdog agency, to study whether there are differences tied to race or ethnicity in VA compensation benefits, VA disability ratings, and the rejection of fully developed claims. The GAO must also recommend ways to collect better data on these differences. It must brief Congress on early results within one year and then submit a final report.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who apply for VA compensation or disability benefits
who_it_affects.how: The study examines whether their race or ethnicity is linked to differences in benefits, ratings, or claim rejections, but the law itself does not change their benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Congress and the Department of Veterans Affairs
who_it_affects.how: They will receive the GAO's briefing and final report and may use its findings and data recommendations in future decisions.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on November 30, 2021, with the initial briefing due within one year and a final report due after that.
